cim: AI in the insurance sector: Why efficiency gains are just the beginning
kihagyva: P3: 40 pont, tendencia 20%, jóváhagyás után fordul
cim_eredeti: AI in the insurance sector: Why efficiency gains are just the beginning
szoveg_eredeti:
Artificial intelligence is already transforming processes at insurance companies, but rarely the business itself. Many applications aim to automate routine tasks, reduce costs or make operations more productive. The step from individual efficiency gains to genuine transformation now lies in using AI to redesign customer processes, decision-making, products and entire business models. Based on the findings of our global study ‘Unlocking AI value in insurance’, which surveyed senior executives from the insurance sector, this publication analyses the gap between the AI ambitions of many companies and the changes actually achieved. It highlights the obstacles standing in the way of successfully realising value and presents a three-horizon model for the AI-driven development of businesses. It also outlines areas of action through which insurers can redesign customer experiences, operational models and business models. The result provides guidance for executives who wish to harness the potential of AI and create sustainable competitive advantages.

Insurers are convinced that artificial intelligence will have a lasting impact on the industry. Even today, AI is helping to assess risks, process claims, manage policies and automate internal processes.

The study is based on an international survey commissioned by KPMG on the role of AI in the further development of insurance companies.

The findings are based on a qualitative and quantitative survey of 44 senior executives from the insurance sector across 20 countries and six regions. In addition, findings from our study ‘Transforming the Enterprise 2026’ – in which 53 executives from the insurance sector took part – were analysed.

Partner, Financial Services, Head of Insurance
